newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Lauder's CME rejects Ukrainian firm's complaint.
newsitem.headline: Lauder's CME rejects Ukrainian firm's complaint.

text.p: Central European Media Enterprises Ltd (CME) said on Monday there was no substance in a $750-million lawsuit launched in New York against CME and its founder Ronald Lauder over its television operation in Ukraine.

"Our attorneys feel it is completely without merit and certainly isn't a situation that belongs in New York," CME's president and chief executive, Leonard Fertig, told a news conference of the case launched by Ukraine's Perekhid Media.
The lawsuit, launched in May against London-based CME and its founder, the heir to the Estee Lauder fortune, alleged CME's Ukrainian partner Studio 1+1 had obtained its licence illegally.
Perekhid lost its licence in the middle of 1996 while Studio 1+1 won a tender for its broadcasting time a few months later.
Studio 1+1 general director Olexander Rodnyansky denied his company used intimidation to obtain its licence.
CME holds television interests in the Czech Republic, Romania, Slovenia, Slovakia, Germany and Poland.
Fertig said CME had already invested more than $20 million in the Ukrainian television market and complained at Perekhid's use of the New York court system to settle Ukrainian problems.
